# Evaluation Results

**Corpus:** the IETF HTTP core standards. RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching) and RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1) total about 92,000 words of normative, heavily cross-referenced text. `scripts/fetch_corpus.py` downloads them and converts them to Markdown with their section structure intact.

**Evaluation set:** `evaluation_dataset.json` has 32 questions, written by hand against the RFC text rather than generated by an LLM:

| Type | Count | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| Lookup | 14 | One fact from one section, e.g. which methods are safe, or the s-maxage rule |
| Multi-Hop | 9 | Facts from two sections, often in different RFCs, e.g. heuristic caching needs RFC 9110 §15.3.1 *and* RFC 9111 §4.2.2 |
| Unanswerable | 5 | Near-domain questions the corpus can't answer (HTTP/2 SETTINGS, WebSocket keys, 429, HSTS, QPACK). Each was checked to be absent from the corpus with grep |
| Ambiguous | 4 | Underspecified questions ("How long can it be cached?") |

Each Lookup and Multi-Hop question lists the RFC sections it depends on and one or more verbatim **evidence** passages. That allows retrieval to be scored exactly, by checking whether the chunks given to the generator contain the passage, with no LLM judge involved. Every evidence passage was verified to occur in the converted corpus.

Earlier results: the pre-change RFC baseline is in [`results/rfc_baseline/RESULTS.md`](results/rfc_baseline/RESULTS.md), and the original Apollo 11 demo corpus in [`results/apollo11/RESULTS.md`](results/apollo11/RESULTS.md).

All runs: 2026-10-03, `gpt-4o-mini` as generator and judge, `text-embedding-3-small`, `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`.

---

## Summary: before vs after

The baseline evaluation produced four recommendations. Each was implemented, then measured, and kept only if the measurements supported it:

| Recommendation | Implemented as | Measured effect | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn the cross-encoder reranker off | `use_reranker=False`. The cross-encoder now only *scores* the final chunks for the confidence gate (`cross_encoder_confidence`) | The reranker still lowered hit@5 with the new chunks. The gate keeps calibrated scores instead of a constant ~0.5 | **Adopted** |
| Strict citation verifier | Claims count as supported only if *every* part is in the cited text | The HSTS hallucination is now refused. Wrongly answered unanswerable/ambiguous questions fell from 4 of 9 to 1 of 9, with no new false refusals (TokenRecursive) | **Adopted** |
| Cap Markdown sections | Sections over `markdown_max_tokens` are split, and continuation pieces carry the heading path | 800 tokens gave the best hybrid-retrieval MRR of the caps tried (0, 400, 800, 1,200). End to end, capped Markdown is the best strategy | **Adopted, and Markdown is now the default chunking** |
| Query decomposition for multi-hop questions | `DecomposingRetriever` (`decompose_queries`) | Multi-hop full@5 moved by at most ±1 of 9 questions, while hit@5 and MRR fell in most configurations | **Implemented but off by default** |

The default configuration before and after (32 questions; LLM-judged metrics are 3-run means):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Configuration | TokenRecursive, hybrid + reranker, lenient verifier | Markdown capped at 800 tokens, hybrid, no reranker, strict verifier |
| Retrieval hit@1 / hit@5 / MRR (exact, 23 answerable) | 0.522 / 0.826 / 0.649 | **0.609 / 0.913 / 0.761** |
| Correctness | 0.902 | **0.971** |
| Faithfulness | 0.970 | **0.975** |
| Citation accuracy | 0.975 | **1.000** |
| Answerable questions refused (single diagnostic run) | 0 / 23 (TokenRecursive) | 1 / 23 (M07, where retrieval misses the evidence) |
| Unanswerable/ambiguous questions answered (single diagnostic run) | 4 / 9, incl. one hallucination | **1 / 9** (A03, a grounded "it depends" answer) |
| Fallback rate | 0.156 | 0.250 |
| Words of context per query | ~1,700 | ~2,100 |

The fallback rate rose because the system now declines unanswerable and ambiguous questions it used to answer. 8 of the 9 that should fall back do so now (only A03 still gets an answer), and only 1 answerable question (M07) is refused. Part of the correctness gain comes from this: answers to those questions used to be included in the average. So the correctness improvement is real, but it is not only better answers to the same questions.

## 1. Retrieval quality: exact scoring against gold evidence

Command: `python scripts/eval_retrieval.py` (36 configurations). Raw data: [`results/retrieval_eval.csv`](results/retrieval_eval.csv). Cap sweep: [`results/retrieval_eval_markdown_cap0.csv`](results/retrieval_eval_markdown_cap0.csv), [`…cap400.csv`](results/retrieval_eval_markdown_cap400.csv), [`…cap1200.csv`](results/retrieval_eval_markdown_cap1200.csv). Covers 23 answerable questions with `final_k = 5`, and no LLM is involved in scoring. With this few questions, one question is worth 0.043 of hit@5.

**Reranker off vs on** (hybrid retrieval, no decomposition):

| Chunking | Reranker | hit@1 | hit@5 | full@5 | MRR | Words to LLM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TokenRecursive | off | 0.522 | 0.957 | 0.652 | 0.721 | 1,666 |
| TokenRecursive | on | 0.522 | 0.826 | 0.652 | 0.649 | 1,681 |
| **Markdown (cap 800)** | **off** | **0.609** | **0.913** | **0.652** | **0.761** | **2,143** |
| Markdown (cap 800) | on | 0.522 | 0.739 | 0.478 | 0.610 | 2,102 |
| Semantic | off | 0.826 | 1.000 | 0.739 | 0.913 | 5,073 |
| Semantic | on | 0.522 | 0.870 | 0.652 | 0.648 | 3,687 |

The reranker lowers hit@5 in every chunking × mode combination again: 9 of 9, as in the baseline.

**Markdown cap sweep** (reranker off, no decomposition):

| Cap (tokens) | Chunks | Sparse hit@1 / hit@5 / MRR | Hybrid hit@1 / hit@5 / MRR | Words to LLM (hybrid) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 248 | 0.739 / 1.000 / 0.851 | 0.565 / 0.870 / 0.710 | 3,700 |
| 1,200 | 294 | 0.870 / 0.957 / 0.900 | 0.609 / 0.870 / 0.713 | 2,780 |
| **800** | 340 | 0.696 / 0.957 / 0.819 | **0.609 / 0.913 / 0.761** | 2,143 |
| 400 | 515 | 0.565 / 0.957 / 0.746 | 0.435 / 0.913 / 0.646 | 1,268 |

Capping helps hybrid retrieval, because whole sections were too long for good embeddings, and it cuts context by 40%. Under hybrid retrieval, the default mode, 800 tokens is the best cap tried. With sparse-only retrieval, 1,200 has the best precision of any configuration measured (hit@1 0.870, MRR 0.900). That suggests sparse-only Markdown could be an option, but the dense/sparse weights were not part of these recommendations and stay at 0.7/0.3.

**Query decomposition off vs on** (reranker off). Multi-hop full@5 is the share of the 9 multi-hop questions with all their evidence in the top 5:

| Chunking | Mode | Multi-hop full@5 (off → on) | hit@5 (off → on) | MRR (off → on) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TokenRecursive | sparse | 0.111 → 0.000 | 0.957 → 0.913 | 0.790 → 0.790 |
| TokenRecursive | hybrid | 0.111 → 0.111 | 0.957 → 0.870 | 0.721 → 0.645 |
| Markdown (cap 800) | sparse | 0.333 → 0.222 | 0.957 → 0.913 | 0.819 → 0.791 |
| Markdown (cap 800) | hybrid | 0.222 → 0.333 | 0.913 → 0.870 | 0.761 → 0.693 |
| Semantic | sparse | 0.333 → 0.333 | 1.000 → 1.000 | 0.884 → 0.878 |
| Semantic | hybrid | 0.333 → 0.444 | 1.000 → 1.000 | 0.913 → 0.838 |

Decomposition splits all 9 multi-hop questions sensibly. But the sub-questions rarely rank the second evidence passage near the top, and fusing 3–4 rankings crowds the original query's best passages out of 5 slots. Multi-hop retrieval is still the largest open problem: the best configuration gets full evidence for only 4 of 9 questions. Larger `final_k`, or retrieval that follows the RFCs' own section cross-references, are the obvious next experiments.

## 2. Chunking strategies end to end (LLM-judged)

Command: `python main.py --runs 3`. Raw data: [`results/strategy_comparison_results.csv`](results/strategy_comparison_results.csv). Every strategy uses the new retrieval defaults (hybrid 0.7/0.3, no reranker, cross-encoder confidence, strict verifier, no decomposition). Each value is the mean ± std over 3 runs of 32 questions.

| Strategy | Correctness | Faithfulness | Retrieval relevance | Citation accuracy | Fallback rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TokenRecursive | 0.947 ± 0.001 | 0.959 ± 0.008 | 0.941 ± 0.003 | 1.000 ± 0.000 | 0.271 ± 0.015 |
| **Markdown (cap 800)** | **0.971 ± 0.003** | 0.975 ± 0.000 | **0.979 ± 0.000** | **1.000 ± 0.000** | **0.250 ± 0.000** |
| Semantic | 0.967 ± 0.005 | **0.987 ± 0.002** | 0.893 ± 0.005 | 0.942 ± 0.012 | 0.375 ± 0.000 |
| *Baseline, for reference* | | | | | |
| TokenRecursive, reranker on, lenient | 0.902 | 0.970 | 0.906 | 0.975 | 0.156 |
| Markdown uncapped, reranker on, lenient | 0.937 | 0.968 | 0.938 | 1.000 | 0.229 |

**Per question** (one diagnostic run of the default pipeline per strategy; 23 answerable and 9 unanswerable/ambiguous):

| Strategy | Before: answerable refused | Before: unanswerable answered | After: answerable refused | After: unanswerable answered | Citations repaired (after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TokenRecursive | 0 | 4 (U04, A01, A02, A03) | 0 | 1 (A03) | 2 |
| Markdown | 2 (L02, M07) | 2 (A01, A03) | 1 (M07) | 1 (A03) | 0 |
| Semantic | not run | not run | 4 (L05, M02, M05, M07) | 1 (A03) | 2 |

- **U04, the HSTS hallucination, is fixed.** The strict verifier rejects a claim that cites the Cache-Control `max-age` text while describing HSTS.
- **A03** ("Is it safe to retry that request automatically?") is still answered, with a grounded "it depends on whether the method is idempotent" explanation. That is arguably the right behaviour.
- **M07** ("resume an interrupted download…") is refused because no configuration retrieves its evidence: a vocabulary gap that dense and sparse retrieval both miss.
- **Semantic** has the highest faithfulness but refuses 4 answerable questions, so it is not the default.

## Caveats

- 32 questions (23 answerable) is a small set. Treat retrieval differences under ~0.04, or LLM-judged differences under ~0.01, as noise.
- The per-question tables come from single diagnostic runs, not the 3-run averages.
- The judge is the same model as the generator, and it is not validated against human labels on this corpus.
- The questions were written while reading the RFCs, which can favour BM25.
- The decision to make Markdown the default was based on the same 32 questions it is evaluated on. There is no held-out set.
